result: No material source defect found in the scoped guard/error/drop-order correction. No tests executed by evaluator.
source_checks: DatabaseLock is private and constructed only after try_lock succeeds. Failed lock acquisition drops only its unsuccessful raw File and cannot invoke this explicit-unlock guard.

Store fields declare Connection before Option<DatabaseLock>. Rust field drop order therefore drops the SQLite connection before unlocking the process-ownership guard; no Store Drop override changes that order.

Errors after acquisition during private-file creation, Connection::open or initialize return through the acquired guard. initialize owns its connection, so its locals drop before the caller acquired guard. No unlocked live Store is returned.
In-memory initialization retains _lock=None. Normal Store API/persistence/schema remain unchanged.

The duplicate-handle regression is unchanged except accessing the new private tuple field. Both original and reopened live-owner exclusion assertions are retained; duplicate stays open during reopening.

retained_reproduction.outcome: Exact-target regression failed once: live Store exclusion succeeded, then reopening after Store drop failed while duplicated OS File stayed open.
retained_reproduction.scope: Demonstrates duplicated-handle lock lifetime; does not trace/prove the exact fork/pre-exec sequence behind the earlier intermittent CLI failure.

limits: File::unlock in Drop is best effort; its Result is ignored to avoid destructor panic. This does not prove release under arbitrary native OS errors.
Source inspection of ordering and retained failed reproduction are not a fixed-test pass, a cross-platform lock semantics proof or a new full-workspace green result. Root owns subsequent checks.
No evaluator tests/builds/native/credential/model/network/GUI executions, implementation edits or public writes. Only this new private receipt proposal was written.
